request.spec:
A DRAFT claim can be deleted (a button on the claim; any other status, or a claim in a closed
period, is refused with an error on the claim): its status becomes DELETED, it counts nowhere (not
in any total, not in the status counts of the header or the summary), it cannot be edited, opened
or voided, its log gains a DELETED line, and CLAIM_DELETED is written naming the claim. On the same
sheet-today it was deleted, a restore button makes it a DRAFT again (CLAIM_RESTORED, a DRAFT line in
the log); on a later day the restore is refused.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A DRAFT claim can be deleted (a button on the claim; any other status, or a claim in a closed
period, is refused with an error on the claim): its status becomes DELETED, it counts nowhere (not
in any total, not in the status counts of the header or the summary), it cannot be edited, opened
or voided, its log gains a DELETED line, and CLAIM_DELETED is written naming the claim. On the same
sheet-today it was deleted, a restore button makes it a DRAFT again (CLAIM_RESTORED, a DRAFT line in
the log); on a later day the restore is refused.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I've added delete and restore for draft claims, and all four tests in `bin/e2e` pass: the new delete/restore test and the three scenarios covering existing features.

**How it works:** `DELETED` is a new claim status. Delete and restore use the existing claim status endpoint: delete moves a DRAFT to `DELETED`, and restore moves it back to `DRAFT`.

- **Delete:** only a DRAFT can be deleted. Any other status is refused with the error on the claim, and so is a claim whose due-by date falls in a closed period, using the same check other status changes already use.
- **Restore:** allowed only on the sheet-today the claim was deleted, going by the last `DELETED` line in its log. On a later day it is refused.
- **What a deleted claim can't do:** it can't be opened or voided, because the status rules don't allow either move. It can't be edited, because editing already requires a DRAFT. Reassigning is blocked too.
- **Totals and counts:** a deleted claim counts nowhere. Totals only include OPEN, PENDING and SETTLED claims, and the header and summary status counts only cover the original five statuses.
- **Log and audit:** each move adds a status-log line (`DELETED …`, then `DRAFT …` on restore). The audit file gets `CLAIM_DELETED` or `CLAIM_RESTORED` with person, amount and date, in the same form as the other claim status events.

**Changes:**
- **Backend:** `ClaimStatus.java` gets the new status and its allowed moves. `CheckClerkLimit.java` gets the same-day restore check. `ClaimLogStore.java` gets a small `lastOn` helper, which the existing settled-date lookup now uses too. I also updated the description comment in `status.POST.yml`.
- **Frontend:** the claim status type in `claims.ts` includes `DELETED`, and `list.slot.tsx` has `claim-delete` and `claim-restore` buttons on each claim row.
- **No database migration:** the status column is a plain string with no list of allowed values.

The request only names edit, open and void as blocked. Most other actions (comments, proofs, split, redate and so on) are not explicitly blocked for a deleted claim, and the tests don't cover them.
